issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot review an eviction controller’s determination of non-payment when the governing scheme empowers the controller to decide that issue and makes the decision final after the prescribed appeal.
material_facts: The tenants’ rent had fallen into arrears, and the landlords sought their eviction on the ground of non-payment.
The Controller found non-payment and ordered eviction; the designated appellate authority upheld the order.
The tenants then brought a civil suit seeking a declaration that the eviction order was illegal and without jurisdiction, arguing that rent had in fact been paid.
The Supreme Court resolved the appeal on the Controller’s authority and the statutory finality of the decision, without deciding whether the rent had actually been paid on time.
issues.conclusion: The civil court could not question the Controller’s determination of non-payment, even if that determination was wrong; the appeal was allowed and the decrees dismissing the tenants’ suit were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 11, 16 and 18(3) of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, the Controller was empowered to determine whether rent had not been paid and, on that finding, to order eviction; the Act provided an appeal to the Commissioner and made the Commissioner’s decision, and subject to it the Controller’s order, final and not open to challenge in court. Where a tribunal is entrusted both with deciding preliminary facts and with acting on its determination of those facts, its decision within that authority cannot be collaterally challenged merely because it may be erroneous. The Court relied on Queen v. Commissioners for Special Purposes of the Income Tax (21 Q.B.D. 313) and Colonial Bank of Australasia v. Willan (L.R. 5 P.C. 417).

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_challenge and controller_empowered_to_determine_default and statutory_appeal_upheld_order and decision_final_against_court_challenge

predicates.rent_control_eviction_challenge: A party brings a civil proceeding to challenge an eviction decision made under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.controller_empowered_to_determine_defaul: The scheme empowers the designated controller to determine whether rent was not paid and to order eviction on that basis.
predicates.statutory_appeal_upheld_order: The designated appellate authority has upheld the controller’s eviction decision.
predicates.decision_final_against_court_challenge: The scheme makes the decision final after the prescribed appeal and bars its challenge in court.

issues.definition: When a civil proceeding challenges a rent-control eviction decision, the controller was empowered to determine default, the prescribed appeal upheld the order, and the decision is final against court challenge, the civil court cannot question the eviction decision.
